correctness.rationale: Reconstructed from actual RESULT.md: im P=H is subalgebra and K=ker P is H-invariant because of the two averaging identities and P²=P. If nonzero H lay in V, a kernel lift of e would bracket with nonzero H into H∩K, impossible. Hence h=e+u lies in H. Since ad_h restricts to identity on V and has kernel F_qh, invariance forces K⊂V, an ideal, so P is a Lie retraction; this holds in characteristic 2. Conversely P(e)=e+v,P|V=Q, Q²=Q,Qv=0 parameterizes all nonzero maps. Count rank r+1 by [m r]_q complements q^{r(m-r)} times v choices q^{m-r}. Centering r=m/2+s gives quadratic exponents -2s²-s (even) and -2s²+s (odd), product factors converge uniformly within |s|≤m/4 and Gaussian tails are exponentially suppressed; zero projection negligible. Independently brute enumerated all q^{n²} matrices for (q,n)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3), directly checking idempotence and original averaging identities, obtaining exactly (1,2,1),(1,4,12,1),(1,3,1),(1,9,36,1).
